overall_note: Rough completion for each phase of the plan. The overall figure is a guess set by hand, not a sum.
machine: 14-inch MacBook Pro, M2 Pro (`T6020`, `apple,j414s`, G14S GPU, 32 GB), Aurora Silicon Linux

gap.lede: How long a second client (a stand-in for the desktop) waits for the GPU while one long compute job runs, on this machine today. Measured with `gpuprobe`, a 16 ms tick beside the compute job.

rows.label: 68 ms
rows.sub: p95 wait with one 6 s compute dispatch; 29% of ticks miss a 120 Hz frame. [data](../data/20261122-ramp-default-preempt-long/)

rows.label: 32 ms
rows.sub: p95 wait with one 3 s dispatch; 35% of ticks over 8.3 ms. [data](../data/20261122-ramp-default-preempt/)

rows.label: 8.3 ms
rows.sub: One frame at 120 Hz. Batched 20 ms dispatches already stay under it (p95 0.72 ms).

phases.name: Research
phases.short: What Aurora Silicon and others already have for Apple GPUs, and what is missing on this chip
phases.summary: Aurora’s kernel, Mesa, `gpubench` and agent guidelines read, plus the Metal-on-Vulkan projects. No Metal API exists for Apple GPUs on Linux, and the kernel turns compute preemption on automatically only for the M2 Max.
done: Kernel source: `compute_preempt` defaults to -1, which means on for chip `0x6021` (M2 Max) only
linux-aurora#25 read: with preemption, M2 Max owners saw 0 timeouts
phases.gate: A plan with a testable first hypothesis.

phases.name: Baseline
phases.short: Record what the GPU does today, before changing anything
phases.summary: Kernel, driver and GPU error history recorded read-only. `gpubench` core chunks ran clean. A compute probe shows the desktop waiting in proportion to compute dispatch length, which fits missing preemption, but it has not reproduced the #2701 timeouts yet.
done: GPU errors in only 2 of 99 boots; the #2701 boot has 116 timeouts
`gpuprobe` ramp: single dispatches of 50 ms to 12 s, batched up to 10 s
next: Reproduce an actual timeout: several clients at once, or memory pressure
A FLUX.2 and an ACE-Step run with `journalctl` counts
phases.gate: A repeatable way to trigger the #2701 timeouts, with its data.

phases.name: Fix the compute timeouts
phases.short: Long Vulkan compute trips GPU timeouts and corrupts the desktop (#2701)
phases.summary: The leading suspect is that firmware compute preemption is off for this chip. The test is planned in [preempt-test.md](preempt-test.md): one boot with `options asahi compute_preempt=1` in `/etc/modprobe.d/`. It needs a reboot of the shared test Mac, so it waits for the S2R work.
done: Found that a modprobe option is enough: no kernel command line change
Test plan with three ways to run it and the way back
next: Boot with `compute_preempt=1` and rerun the ramp and the real workloads
Qualify per linux-aurora#25: repeated digests, throughput, compositor concurrency, teardown
Decide the right rule without a chip gate, draft the patch, report into #2701
phases.gate: 0 timeouts under the #2701 workloads, results correct, throughput cost known.

phases.name: Measure against macOS
phases.short: The same benchmarks on macOS (Metal) and Linux (Vulkan) on this machine
phases.summary: No `gpubench` record exists for this chip on macOS. Boot macOS on this Mac, record the suite with the Metal executor, and rank the rows where Linux loses with `tools/performance-gate.py`.
phases.gate: A ranked list of the rows where Linux is slower, with real workloads beside the synthetic ones.

phases.name: Close the gaps
phases.short: Scheduling, compiler and memory work driven by phase 3
phases.summary: Each gap from phase 3 becomes its own fix with before and after numbers: compute against compositor scheduling, Borealis compiler and dispatch performance, memory.
phases.gate: Linux at or above macOS on every comparable row.

pieces.name: Compute preemption
pieces.known: Automatic only for M2 Max (`0x6021`). On this kernel `compute_preempt` exists (`modinfo`) but has no sysfs file.

pieces.name: #2701 timeouts
pieces.known: 116 timeouts in the reporting boot. Not reproduced by a single synthetic dispatch of up to 12 s.

pieces.name: Desktop beside compute
pieces.known: The second client’s p95 wait grows from 2.9 ms (50 ms dispatch) to 69 ms (12 s). Batched work stays under 1 ms.

pieces.known: linux-aurora#335 faults on M1 were fixed in 7.3.0-2-20261110.1. Not checked on t6020.

prior_art.name: linux-aurora#25
prior_art.what: G14X compute preemption: automatic on M2 Max, opt-in on Pro and Ultra pending qualification. 0 timeouts with it on M2 Max; about 1% throughput cost there, 12 to 20% on M1 decode.

prior_art.name: linux-aurora#389
prior_art.what: M3 Pro: long compute delays the compositor 40 to 200 ms. The fix caps compute batch time while another client waits. Different backend from G14X.

prior_art.name: linux-aurora#440
prior_art.what: G15C: llama.cpp prefill trips the compute deadline and the GPU fail-stops until reboot.

prior_art.name: gpubench
prior_art.what: Matched Vulkan and Metal benchmarks and a gate: Linux must beat the macOS reference on every comparable row.

prior_art.name: metal2vulkan
prior_art.what: A Metal runtime on Vulkan. Its docs already list Honeykrisp on the M2 Pro as missing raster-order access and pixel interlock.

findings.title: Compute preemption is off on the M2 Pro
findings.body: The kernel turns it on automatically only for chip `0x6021`. Without it the firmware cannot switch compute out for another client, and on G14X it kills the work when its timeouts expire.

findings.title: The desktop waits in proportion to the compute dispatch
findings.body: One dispatch of 50 ms gives a p95 wait of 2.9 ms; 3 s gives 32 ms; 6 to 12 s gives 68 to 69 ms, with up to 35% of 16 ms ticks over a 120 Hz frame.

findings.title: Dispatch boundaries are switch points
findings.body: The same work as 20 ms dispatches in one submission keeps the p95 wait at 0.72 to 0.79 ms. Only a single long kernel hurts.

findings.title: A long dispatch alone does not time out
findings.body: No timeout up to a 12 s synthetic dispatch. The #2701 boot had 116 under llama.cpp-style load, so the trigger likely needs more than one client or memory pressure.

findings.title: GPU errors are rare outside #2701
findings.body: 2 of 99 boots in the journal. The other one is a single timeout right after a global out-of-memory kill.

findings.title: A modprobe option is enough for the test
findings.body: `asahi` is a module and `modinfo` lists `compute_preempt`, so `options asahi compute_preempt=1` works at boot. The kernel command line stays default.

rules: Log a boot-affecting step in the worklog first, with the way back.
No GPU test reboot without the S2R work’s go-ahead: the Mac is shared.
Every number in `docs/` points at a folder in `data/`.
`journalctl -k` reads only the current boot. Use `-t kernel` to count across boots.
The harness writes results to `data/` itself, not only to a terminal that may die.
Fix the cause with the default command line, and no chip or board gates.
unknowns: Whether `compute_preempt=1` stops the #2701 timeouts on t6020.
What it costs in throughput on the M2 Pro.
What triggers the #2701 timeouts, since a single 12 s dispatch does not.
How far Borealis is from Metal on this chip, per workload.
Whether the linux-aurora#335 kill and teardown fault also applies to t6020.
